questions.questionText: A surveyor standing 80 m from the foot of a vertical tower observes its top at an angle of elevation of 60°. What is the length of the line of sight from the surveyor's position to the top of the tower?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The horizontal distance is the adjacent side, so cos 60° = 80 / L and L = 80 / cos 60° = 160 m.

questions.questionText: Standing on level ground, a student is 45 m from the foot of a vertical water tank tower and finds the angle of elevation of its top to be 30°. What is the height of the water tank tower?
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle, tan 30° = height / horizontal distance, so height = 45 x tan 30° = 45 x 1/√3 = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: Standing at a point on level ground, a student finds the angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower to be 60°. On walking 48 m directly away from the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 30°. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanationText: With height h, the distances from the foot are h/√3 and h√3. The difference equals the distance walked: h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 48, so h = 24√3 m.

questions.questionText: Two vertical towers of heights 25 m and 85 m stand on the same horizontal ground. From the top of the shorter tower the angle of elevation of the top of the taller tower is 60°. Find the distance between the towers.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. questions.questionText: From a point 87 m away on level ground, the top of a vertical temple gopuram subtends an angle of elevation of 60° at the eye of an observer standing at ground level. Find its height.

questions.questionText: An observer at the top of a 96 m high hotel terrace sees a rickshaw on the level ground below at an angle of depression of 30°. Find the horizontal distance of the rickshaw from the foot of the structure.
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation measured from the rickshaw, so tan 30° = 96 / d and d = 96 / 1/√3 = 96√3 m.

questions.questionText: At a certain moment a 6 m high pole casts a shadow 4 m long. At the same moment a nearby tree casts a shadow 10 m long on level ground. What is the height of the tree?
questions.explanationText: The sun's rays make the same angle, so the two right triangles are similar: h / 10 = 6 / 4. Hence h = 6 x 10 / 4 = 15 m.

questions.questionText: The top of a vertical post of height 14 m is observed from a point 14√3 m away from its foot on level ground. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the post from that point.

questions.questionText: A tree is broken by the wind so that the broken part bends and its top touches the ground, making an angle of 60° with the ground at a point 9 m from the foot of the tree. What was the original height of the tree?
questions.explanationText: The standing part is 9 tan 60° = 9√3 m and the broken part is 9 / cos 60° = 18 m. The original height is their sum, (9√3 + 18) m.

questions.questionText: Two points A and B lie on level ground in a straight line with the foot of a vertical factory chimney, on the same side of it, with B nearer to the factory chimney. If AB = 100 m and the angles of elevation of the top of the factory chimney from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively, find the height of the factory chimney.

questions.questionText: A guy rope runs from the top of a vertical pole 14 m high to a peg on the ground 48 m from the foot of the pole. Assuming the rope is straight and taut, how long is the rope?

The rope is the hypotenuse of a right triangle, so L^2 = 15^2 + 20^2 = 625 and L = 25 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 45 m high lighthouse, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 60°. How far has the ship sailed during this interval?
questions.explanationText: The two distances from the foot are 45√3 m and 45/√3 m. The ship has covered 45√3 - 45/√3 = 2 x 45/√3 = 30√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical pole 48 m high casts a shadow on level ground that is 1/√3 times its height. What is the sun's angle of elevation at that moment?
questions.explanationText: The pole is the opposite side and the shadow the adjacent side, so tan θ = height / shadow = 48 / 16√3 = √3. This is the tangent of 60°, so the sun's elevation is 60°.

questions.questionText: A vertical chimney is 60 m high and a point on level ground is 20√3 m from its foot. What is the angle of elevation of the top of the chimney from that point?
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle, tan θ = height / horizontal distance = 60 / 20√3 , which simplifies to √3. This is the tangent of the standard angle 60°, so the angle of elevation is 60°.

questions.questionText: A ladder 36 m long rests against a wall making an angle of 30° with the ground. It is then re-set so that it makes an angle of 60° with the ground, its foot being moved closer to the wall. By how much does the top of the ladder now reach higher on the wall?
questions.explanationText: At 30° the ladder reaches 36 sin30° = 18 m and at 60° it reaches 36 sin60° = 18√3 m. The extra height is the difference, (18√3 - 18) m.

questions.questionText: At the same time of day, two poles of heights 12 m and 18 m cast shadows on level ground. If the shorter one casts a shadow 16 m long, how long is the shadow of the taller one?

questions.questionText: A vertical stick 3 m long casts a shadow 5 m long on level ground. At the same moment a nearby tower is 45 m high. What is the length of the tower's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Shadows are proportional to heights, so S / 45 = 5 / 3, giving S = 75 m.

questions.questionText: Under the same sunlight a 24 m tall tower has a shadow 9 m long while a antenna standing close by has a shadow 27 m long. How tall is the antenna?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Similar right triangles give h / 27 = 24 / 9, so h = 72 m.

questions.questionText: At the same time of day, two trees of heights 9 m and 21 m cast shadows on level ground. If the shorter one casts a shadow 16 m long, how long is the shadow of the taller one?
questions.explanationText: The sun's elevation is the same, so shadows are proportional to heights: s/16 = 21/9, giving s = 112/3 m.

questions.questionText: A street lamp is fixed at a height of 12 m. A person 3 m tall stands 10 m away from the foot of the lamp post on level ground. How long is the person's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By similar triangles, s / 3 = (s + 10) / 12, which gives 12 s = 3(s + 10) and s = 10/3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical stick 1.5 m long casts a shadow 2 m long on level ground. At the same moment a nearby tower is 30 m high. What is the length of the tower's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Shadows are proportional to heights, so S / 30 = 2 / 1.5, giving S = 40 m.

questions.questionText: Two points A and B lie on level ground in a straight line with the foot of a vertical cliff face, on the same side of it, with B nearer to the cliff face. If AB = 36 m and the angles of elevation of the top of the cliff face from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively, find the height of the cliff face.
questions.explanationText: If h is the height, the foot distances are h/tan30° = h√3 and h/tan60° = h/√3. Their difference is AB: h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 36, so h = 36√3/2 = 18√3 m.

questions.questionText: From a point 51 m away on level ground, the top of a vertical stone pillar subtends an angle of elevation of 60° at the eye of an observer standing at ground level. Find its height.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Height = 51 x tan 60° = 51 x √3 = 51√3 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 30 m high building, the angles of depression of two cars standing in a straight line on the same side of the building are 45° and 30°. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanationText: The nearer object is at 30/tan45° = 30 m and the farther one at 30/tan30° = 30√3 m. The distance between them is 30√3 - 30 = (30√3 - 30) m.

questions.questionText: A street lamp is fixed at a height of 10 m. A person 2 m tall stands 16 m away from the foot of the lamp post on level ground. How long is the person's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By similar triangles, s / 2 = (s + 16) / 10, which gives 10 s = 2(s + 16) and s = 4 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 90 m high hill-top post, the angle of depression of a bus standing on level ground is 60°. How far is the bus from the foot of the structure?
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the bus, since the horizontal lines are parallel. Hence tan 60° = 90 / d, so d = 90 / √3 = 30√3 m.

questions.questionText: A 30 m long ladder leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the level ground. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Here the ladder is the hypotenuse, so sin 60° = height / 30, giving height = 30 x sin 60° = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 20 m high office block, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower standing on the same level ground is 30°, and the horizontal distance between the two structures is 30 m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanationText: Above the level of the roof, the tower rises 30 x tan30° = 10√3 m. Adding the 20 m of the office block gives a total height of (10√3 + 20) m.

questions.questionText: A person on level ground observes the top of a vertical pole at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 25 m straight towards the foot of the pole, the angle of elevation becomes 45°. Find the height of the pole.
questions.explanationText: Let h be the height. The two foot distances are h√3 and h, and their difference is the distance walked: h√3 - h = 25. Hence h = 25/(√3 - 1) = 25(√3 + 1)/2 = (12.5√3 + 12.5) m.

questions.questionText: Two vertical towers stand on level ground 45 m apart. From the top of the shorter tower, which is 18 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of the taller tower is 30°. Find the height of the taller tower.
questions.explanationText: The horizontal line from the top of the shorter tower gives tan 30° = (H - 18)/45, so H = 18 + 45 x 1/√3 = (15√3 + 18) m.

questions.questionText: At a certain moment a 18 m high tower casts a shadow 12 m long. At the same moment a nearby antenna mast casts a shadow 30 m long on level ground. What is the height of the antenna mast?
questions.explanationText: The sun's rays make the same angle, so the two right triangles are similar: h / 30 = 18 / 12. Hence h = 18 x 30 / 12 = 45 m.

questions.questionText: From a point 45 m from the foot of a vertical building on level ground, the angle of elevation of its top is 53°. Taking tan 53° = 4/3, find the height of the building.
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle formed by the building, the ground and the line of sight, the height is the opposite side and 45 m is the adjacent side. Height = 45 x tan 53° = 45 x 4/3 = 60 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 60 m high cliff, the angle of depression of a boat standing on level ground is 60°. How far is the boat from the foot of the structure?
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the boat, since the horizontal lines are parallel. Hence tan 60° = 60 / d, so d = 60 / √3 = 20√3 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 45 m high headland overlooking the sea, the angle of depression of a boat moving straight towards the shore changes from 45° to 60°. Find the distance covered by the boat.
questions.explanationText: The distances from the foot are 45/tan45° = 45 m and 45/tan60° = 15√3 m. The boat has covered 45 - 15√3 m = (45 - 15√3) m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 36 m high hill-top tower, the angles of depression of two jeeps standing in a straight line on the same side of the hill-top tower are 45° and 30°. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanationText: The nearer object is at 36/tan45° = 36 m and the farther one at 36/tan30° = 36√3 m. The distance between them is 36√3 - 36 = (36√3 - 36) m.

questions.questionText: An observer at the top of a 84 m high ship's mast top sees a life raft on the level ground below at an angle of depression of 60°. Find the horizontal distance of the life raft from the foot of the structure.
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation measured from the life raft, so tan 60° = 84 / d and d = 84 / √3 = 28√3 m.

questions.questionText: An observer on level ground is 120 m, measured horizontally, from the vertical line along which a balloon rises. The angle of elevation of the balloon increases from 30° to 45°. How much has the balloon risen during this interval?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The two heights are 120 tan 30° = 40√3 m and 120 tan 45° = 120 m, so the rise is (120 - 40√3) m.

questions.questionText: Two poles of equal height stand on opposite sides of a 60 m wide street. From a point on the street between them the angles of elevation of their tops are 30° and 60°. Find the common height of the poles.
questions.explanationText: If the point is x m from the first pole, h = x tan30° = (60 - x) tan60°. Solving gives x = 45 m and h = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: A guy rope runs from the top of a vertical pole 21 m high to a peg on the ground 28 m from the foot of the pole. Assuming the rope is straight and taut, how long is the rope?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The rope is the hypotenuse of a right triangle, so L^2 = 21^2 + 28^2 = 1225 and L = 35 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 90 m high cliff, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 60°. How far has the ship sailed during this interval?
questions.explanationText: The two distances from the foot are 90√3 m and 90/√3 m. The ship has covered 90√3 - 90/√3 = 2 x 90/√3 = 60√3 m.

questions.questionText: A street lamp is fixed at a height of 8 m. A person 2 m tall stands 9 m away from the foot of the lamp post on level ground. How long is the person's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By similar triangles, s / 2 = (s + 9) / 8, which gives 8 s = 2(s + 9) and s = 3 m.

questions.questionText: A drone hovers 36 m vertically above a point on the ground that is 48 m horizontally from an observer. What is the straight-line distance between the observer and the drone?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The line of sight is the hypotenuse: L^2 = 36^2 + 48^2 = 3600, so L = 60 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 25 m high building, the angle of depression of a jeep standing on level ground is 30°. How far is the jeep from the foot of the structure?
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the jeep, since the horizontal lines are parallel. Hence tan 30° = 25 / d, so d = 25 / 1/√3 = 25√3 m.

questions.questionText: A person on level ground observes the top of a vertical building at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 30 m straight towards the foot of the building, the angle of elevation becomes 45°. Find the height of the building.
questions.explanationText: Let h be the height. The two foot distances are h√3 and h, and their difference is the distance walked: h√3 - h = 30. Hence h = 30/(√3 - 1) = 30(√3 + 1)/2 = (15√3 + 15) m.

questions.questionText: Standing on level ground, a trainee is 90 m from the foot of a vertical observation tower and finds the angle of elevation of its top to be 30°. What is the height of the observation tower?
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle, tan 30° = height / horizontal distance, so height = 90 x tan 30° = 90 x 1/√3 = 30√3 m.

questions.questionText: An observer on level ground is 60 m, measured horizontally, from the vertical line along which a balloon rises. The angle of elevation of the balloon increases from 30° to 60°. How much has the balloon risen during this interval?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The two heights are 60 tan 30° = 20√3 m and 60 tan 60° = 60√3 m, so the rise is 40√3 m.

questions.questionText: The summit of a mountain peak is 120 m above the surrounding plain. A road runs straight towards the foot of the mountain peak. At what horizontal distance from the foot is the point on the road where the angle of elevation of the summit is 60°?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. tan 60° = 120 / d gives d = 120 / √3 = 40√3 m.

questions.questionText: A drone hovers 30 m vertically above a point on the ground that is 40 m horizontally from an observer. What is the straight-line distance between the observer and the drone?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The line of sight is the hypotenuse: L^2 = 30^2 + 40^2 = 2500, so L = 50 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 120 m high chimney, the angle of depression of the foot of a second vertical structure standing on the same level ground is 60°. How far apart are the two structures?
questions.explanationText: The depression angle equals the elevation angle from the foot of the second structure, so tan 60° = 120 / d and d = 120 / √3 = 40√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical temple tower 24 m high stands on the bank of a river. From a point exactly opposite on the other bank, the angle of elevation of its top is 30°. Find the width of the river.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The river width is the horizontal distance, so tan 30° = 24 / w and w = 24 / 1/√3 = 24√3 m.

questions.questionText: A person on level ground observes the top of a vertical tower at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 20 m straight towards the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanationText: Let h be the height. The two foot distances are h√3 and h, and their difference is the distance walked: h√3 - h = 20. Hence h = 20/(√3 - 1) = 20(√3 + 1)/2 = (10√3 + 10) m.

questions.questionText: A ladder 18 m long rests against a wall making an angle of 30° with the ground. It is then re-set so that it makes an angle of 60° with the ground, its foot being moved closer to the wall. By how much does the top of the ladder now reach higher on the wall?
questions.explanationText: At 30° the ladder reaches 18 sin30° = 9 m and at 60° it reaches 18 sin60° = 9√3 m. The extra height is the difference, (9√3 - 9) m.

questions.questionText: The sun's altitude (angle of elevation) is 60°. How long is the shadow cast on level ground by a vertical chimney of height 42 m?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. With tan 60° = height / shadow, shadow = 42 / tan 60° = 42 / √3 = 14√3 m.

questions.questionText: A antenna cable of length 60 m runs from a point on the ground to the top of a vertical mast and makes an angle of 30° with the ground. How high is the point of attachment above the ground?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Using sin 30° = h / 60, h = 60 x sin 30° = 30 m.

questions.questionText: Two vertical towers stand on level ground 40 m apart. From the top of the shorter tower, which is 20 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of the taller tower is 30°. Find the height of the taller tower.
questions.explanationText: The horizontal line from the top of the shorter tower gives tan 30° = (H - 20)/40, so H = 20 + 40 x 1/√3 = (40/3√3 + 20) m.

questions.questionText: A surveyor standing 45 m from the foot of a vertical pole observes its top at an angle of elevation of 30°. What is the length of the line of sight from the surveyor's position to the top of the pole?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The horizontal distance is the adjacent side, so cos 30° = 45 / L and L = 45 / cos 30° = 30√3 m.

questions.questionText: From a point 75 m from the foot of a building on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the building is 30° and that of the top of a lightning rod standing on the building is 60°. Find the height of the lightning rod.
questions.explanationText: Height of the building = 75 x tan30° = 25√3 m. Height up to the top of the lightning rod = 75 x tan60° = 75√3 m. The lightning rod is the difference, 50√3 m.

questions.questionText: The shadow of a vertical pole on level ground is found to be 30 m longer when the sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. What is the height of the pole?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The two shadows are h√3 and h/√3, so h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 30. Hence h = 30√3/2 = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: A motorist driving along a straight level road towards a vertical chimney notes that the angle of elevation of its top is 30°. After travelling 90 m further towards it, the angle becomes 45°. Find the height of the chimney.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Let h be the height. Then h√3 - h = 90, so h = 90/(√3 - 1) = 90(√3 + 1)/2 = (45√3 + 45) m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 75 m high observation deck, the angle of depression of a van standing on level ground is 30°. How far is the van from the foot of the structure?
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the van, since the horizontal lines are parallel. Hence tan 30° = 75 / d, so d = 75 / 1/√3 = 75√3 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 45 m high cliff, the angles of depression of two boats standing in a straight line on the same side of the cliff are 45° and 30°. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanationText: The nearer object is at 45/tan45° = 45 m and the farther one at 45/tan30° = 45√3 m. The distance between them is 45√3 - 45 = (45√3 - 45) m.

questions.questionText: The top of a vertical pole of height 40 m is observed from a point 40 m away from its foot on level ground. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the pole from that point.
questions.explanationText: The height is the opposite side and the given distance the adjacent side, so tan θ = 40 / 40 = 1, which corresponds to the standard angle θ = 45°.

questions.questionText: The sun's altitude (angle of elevation) is 30°. How long is the shadow cast on level ground by a vertical tree of height 15 m?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. With tan 30° = height / shadow, shadow = 15 / tan 30° = 15 / 1/√3 = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: A ladder 26 m long rests against a wall making an angle of 30° with the ground. It is then re-set so that it makes an angle of 60° with the ground, its foot being moved closer to the wall. By how much does the top of the ladder now reach higher on the wall?
questions.explanationText: At 30° the ladder reaches 26 sin30° = 13 m and at 60° it reaches 26 sin60° = 13√3 m. The extra height is the difference, (13√3 - 13) m.

questions.questionText: A 26 m long ladder is placed against a vertical wall so that its top reaches a point 24 m above the ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By the Pythagorean theorem, d^2 = 26^2 - 24^2 = 100, so d = 10 m.

questions.questionText: At a certain moment a 9 m high pole casts a shadow 6 m long. At the same moment a nearby pole casts a shadow 10 m long on level ground. What is the height of the pole?
questions.explanationText: The sun's rays make the same angle, so the two right triangles are similar: h / 10 = 9 / 6. Hence h = 9 x 10 / 6 = 15 m.

questions.questionText: A person on level ground observes the top of a vertical water tank at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 45 m straight towards the foot of the water tank, the angle of elevation becomes 45°. Find the height of the water tank.
questions.explanationText: Let h be the height. The two foot distances are h√3 and h, and their difference is the distance walked: h√3 - h = 45. Hence h = 45/(√3 - 1) = 45(√3 + 1)/2 = (22.5√3 + 22.5) m.

questions.questionText: Two vertical towers stand on level ground 36 m apart. From the top of the shorter tower, which is 12 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of the taller tower is 30°. Find the height of the taller tower.
questions.explanationText: The horizontal line from the top of the shorter tower gives tan 30° = (H - 12)/36, so H = 12 + 36 x 1/√3 = (12√3 + 12) m.

questions.questionText: Two points A and B lie on level ground in a straight line with the foot of a vertical mast, on the same side of it, with B nearer to the mast. If AB = 24 m and the angles of elevation of the top of the mast from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively, find the height of the mast.
questions.explanationText: If h is the height, the foot distances are h/tan30° = h√3 and h/tan60° = h/√3. Their difference is AB: h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 24, so h = 24√3/2 = 12√3 m.

questions.questionText: On level ground, a painter stands 78 m from the foot of a vertical hoarding frame and measures the angle of elevation of its top as 60°. Calculate the height of the hoarding frame.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Using tan 60° = height / 78, the height is 78 x √3 = 78√3 m.

questions.questionText: A surveyor on a platform 45 m above the valley floor sights the top of a 25 m high marker post on the valley floor at an angle of depression of 30°. What is the horizontal distance between the platform and the post?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The sight line drops 45 - 25 = 20 m, so tan 30° = 20 / d and d = 20√3 m.

questions.questionText: The angles of elevation of the top of a vertical clock tower from two points on level ground in line with its foot and on the same side are 30° and 60°. If the two points are 72 m apart, what is the height of the clock tower?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. With height h, the foot distances are h√3 and h/√3, and h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 72. Hence h = 36√3 m.

questions.questionText: An observer whose eye is 1.5 m above the ground sees the top of a vertical tower at an angle of elevation of 45°. After walking 30 m straight towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanationText: Measured above eye level the tower rises (15√3 + 45) m, obtained from the usual two-angle relation with a walk of 30 m. Adding the eye height 1.5 m gives a total height of (15√3 + 46.5) m.

questions.questionText: Two poles of equal height stand on opposite sides of a 80 m wide canal. From a point on the canal between them the angles of elevation of their tops are 30° and 60°. Find the common height of the poles.
questions.explanationText: If the point is x m from the first pole, h = x tan30° = (80 - x) tan60°. Solving gives x = 60 m and h = 20√3 m.

questions.questionText: A 20 m long ladder leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 30° with the level ground. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Here the ladder is the hypotenuse, so sin 30° = height / 20, giving height = 20 x sin 30° = 10 m.

questions.questionText: On level ground, a cadet stands 75 m from the foot of a vertical radio mast and measures the angle of elevation of its top as 30°. Calculate the height of the radio mast.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Using tan 30° = height / 75, the height is 75 x 1/√3 = 25√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical mast is 18 m high and a point on level ground is 18√3 m from its foot. What is the angle of elevation of the top of the mast from that point?
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle, tan θ = height / horizontal distance = 18 / 18√3 , which simplifies to 1/√3. This is the tangent of the standard angle 30°, so the angle of elevation is 30°.

questions.questionText: A tree is broken by the wind so that the broken part bends and its top touches the ground, making an angle of 45° with the ground at a point 12 m from the foot of the tree. What was the original height of the tree?
questions.explanationText: The standing part is 12 tan 45° = 12 m and the broken part is 12 / cos 45° = 12√2 m. The original height is their sum, (12√2 + 12) m.

questions.questionText: The tops of two vertical masts, 8 m and 28 m high, standing 15 m apart on level ground, are to be connected by a straight cable. What length of cable is required?
questions.explanationText: The cable is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 20 m and 15 m, so L = sqrt(20^2 + 15^2) = 25 m.

questions.questionText: An observer whose eye is 1.5 m above the ground sees the top of a vertical tower at an angle of elevation of 30°. After walking 20 m straight towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanationText: Measured above eye level the tower rises (10√3 + 10) m, obtained from the usual two-angle relation with a walk of 20 m. Adding the eye height 1.5 m gives a total height of (10√3 + 11.5) m.

questions.questionText: Two points A and B lie on level ground in a straight line with the foot of a vertical pillar, on the same side of it, with B nearer to the pillar. If AB = 16 m and the angles of elevation of the top of the pillar from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively, find the height of the pillar.
questions.explanationText: If h is the height, the foot distances are h/tan30° = h√3 and h/tan60° = h/√3. Their difference is AB: h√3 - h/√3 = 2h/√3 = 16, so h = 16√3/2 = 8√3 m.

questions.questionText: A ladder 18 m long rests against a vertical wall, making an angle of 30° with the horizontal ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. The distance from the wall is the adjacent side, so cos 30° = d / 18 and d = 18 x cos 30° = 9√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical stick 2 m long casts a shadow 3 m long on level ground. At the same moment a nearby tower is 24 m high. What is the length of the tower's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Shadows are proportional to heights, so S / 24 = 3 / 2, giving S = 36 m.

questions.questionText: An observer whose eye level is 1.6 m above the ground stands 15 m away from a vertical building. The angle of elevation of the top of the building from the observer's eye is 60°. Find the height of the building.
questions.explanationText: Above eye level the height is 15 x tan 60° = 15√3 m. Adding the eye height 1.6 m gives the total height (15√3 + 1.6) m.

questions.questionText: Two poles of equal height stand on opposite sides of a 20 m wide lane. From a point on the lane between them the angles of elevation of their tops are 30° and 60°. Find the common height of the poles.

questions.questionText: A person standing on the roof of a 40 m high building observes the top of a 25 m high tree standing on the same level ground at an angle of depression of 30°. How far is the tree from the building?
questions.explanationText: The vertical drop from the observer to the top of the tree is 40 - 25 = 15 m, so tan 30° = 15 / d and d = 15√3 m.

questions.questionText: At a certain moment a 5 m high boy's stick casts a shadow 4 m long. At the same moment a nearby lamp post casts a shadow 16 m long on level ground. What is the height of the lamp post?
questions.explanationText: The sun's rays make the same angle, so the two right triangles are similar: h / 16 = 5 / 4. Hence h = 5 x 16 / 4 = 20 m.

questions.questionText: The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower from a point P on level ground is 45°. From a point Q, 20 m nearer the foot of the tower on the same straight line, the angle of elevation is 60°. Determine the height of the tower.

Two vertical towers stand on level ground 60 m apart. From the top of the shorter tower, which is 25 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of the taller tower is 60°. Find the height of the taller tower.
questions.explanationText: The horizontal line from the top of the shorter tower gives tan 60° = (H - 25)/60, so H = 25 + 60 x √3 = (60√3 + 25) m.

questions.questionText: The foot of a ladder is 20 m away from the base of a vertical wall and its top reaches a window 21 m above the ground. What is the length of the ladder?
questions.explanationText: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, so L^2 = 20^2 + 21^2 = 841, giving L = 29 m.

questions.questionText: Two poles of equal height stand on opposite sides of a 40 m wide road. From a point on the road between them the angles of elevation of their tops are 30° and 60°. Find the common height of the poles.
questions.explanationText: If the point is x m from the first pole, h = x tan30° = (40 - x) tan60°. Solving gives x = 30 m and h = 10√3 m.

questions.questionText: A street lamp is fixed at a height of 9 m. A person 2 m tall stands 12 m away from the foot of the lamp post on level ground. How long is the person's shadow?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By similar triangles, s / 2 = (s + 12) / 9, which gives 9 s = 2(s + 12) and s = 24/7 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical pole 36 m high casts a shadow on level ground that is equal to its height. What is the sun's angle of elevation at that moment?
questions.explanationText: The pole is the opposite side and the shadow the adjacent side, so tan θ = height / shadow = 36 / 36 = 1. This is the tangent of 45°, so the sun's elevation is 45°.

questions.questionText: The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical hoarding from a point P on level ground is 45°. From a point Q, 40 m nearer the foot of the hoarding on the same straight line, the angle of elevation is 60°. Determine the height of the hoarding.

The summit of a ridge is 150 m above the surrounding plain. A road runs straight towards the foot of the ridge. At what horizontal distance from the foot is the point on the road where the angle of elevation of the summit is 30°?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. tan 30° = 150 / d gives d = 150 / 1/√3 = 150√3 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 48 m high terrace, the angle of depression of a boy standing on level ground is 30°. How far is the boy from the foot of the structure?
questions.explanationText: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the boy, since the horizontal lines are parallel. Hence tan 30° = 48 / d, so d = 48 / 1/√3 = 48√3 m.

questions.questionText: The tops of two vertical masts, 11 m and 35 m high, standing 7 m apart on level ground, are to be connected by a straight cable. What length of cable is required?
questions.explanationText: The cable is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 24 m and 7 m, so L = sqrt(24^2 + 7^2) = 25 m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 24 m high tower the angles of depression of two vehicles on level ground, lying on opposite sides of the tower and in the same straight line with its foot, are 60° and 45°. How far apart are the two vehicles?
questions.explanationText: Their distances from the foot are 8√3 m and 24 m. Since they are on opposite sides, the separation is the sum, (8√3 + 24) m.

questions.questionText: The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower from a point on level ground is 45°. On moving 26 m directly away from the foot along the same straight line, the angle becomes 30°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanationText: If h is the height, the two distances are h and h√3, and h√3 - h = 26. Hence h = 26/(√3 - 1) = 26(√3 + 1)/2 = (13√3 + 13) m.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 120 m high lighthouse, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 60°. How far has the ship sailed during this interval?
questions.explanationText: The two distances from the foot are 120√3 m and 120/√3 m. The ship has covered 120√3 - 120/√3 = 2 x 120/√3 = 80√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical mast is 96 m high. From a point on level ground the angle of elevation of its top is 53°. Using tan 53° = 4/3, how far is that point from the foot of the mast?
questions.explanationText: Here the height is the opposite side and the required distance is the adjacent side, so distance = height / tan 53° = 96 / (4/3) = 72 m.

questions.questionText: A 17 m long ladder is placed against a vertical wall so that its top reaches a point 15 m above the ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. By the Pythagorean theorem, d^2 = 17^2 - 15^2 = 64, so d = 8 m.

questions.questionText: On level ground, a groundsman stands 54 m from the foot of a vertical stadium floodlight and measures the angle of elevation of its top as 60°. Calculate the height of the stadium floodlight.
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Using tan 60° = height / 54, the height is 54 x √3 = 54√3 m.

questions.questionText: A vertical tower is 50 m high and a point on level ground is 50/3√3 m from its foot. What is the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from that point?
questions.explanationText: In the right triangle, tan θ = height / horizontal distance = 50 / 50/3√3 , which simplifies to √3. This is the tangent of the standard angle 60°, so the angle of elevation is 60°.

questions.questionText: The shadow of a vertical pole on level ground is 54 m long when the sun's altitude is 30°. What is the height of the pole?
questions.explanationText: The vertical height, the horizontal distance along the ground and the line of sight together form a right triangle, so the required quantity follows from the appropriate trigonometric ratio. Height = shadow x tan 30° = 54 x 1/√3 = 18√3 m.
